item.title: Keras LSTM Configurations: Many-to-Many, One-to-Many, and Stateful Sequence Modeling
item.description:
“Keras LSTM Configurations: Many-to-Many, One-to-Many, and Stateful Sequence Modeling”

The behavior of Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) layers like LSTM in Keras fundamentally relies on how the input sequences are structured and how the return_sequences parameter is set.

Keras LSTM Input Data Structure Example

Consider an input scenario involving $N$ oil tanks monitored over 5 hourly time steps, recording two features: Pressure (P) and Temperature (T).

The standard input array shape for this data, representing $N$ sequences of 5 steps each with 2 features per step, is structured as: $$(N, \text{steps}, \text{features}) \rightarrow (N, 5, 2)$$

item.title: Solved: How to Avoid 'CUDA Out of Memory' in PyTorch
item.description:
When working with deep learning models in PyTorch, encountering the infamous RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory error is a common hurdle, especially when using machines with limited GPU memory. This error typically gives a message like:

CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate X MiB (GPU X; X GiB total capacity; X GiB already allocated; X MiB free; X cached)

Such errors can be frustrating when trying to process images or train large models efficiently. Below are some compelling strategies to effectively manage GPU memory usage and avoid this error while training your deep learning models.
